html:
SMTO-SYS-0005 — Connection failed

GUID: b3471116-8764-47e9-a4f8-65e1c32a3861
Slug: transport-connection-failure
Domain: SYS · Subsystem: runtime

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't reach the AI model it uses to work on your request, so it stopped the task. Work the task already finished is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to the network, and that the model server or service is switched on and reachable. SMTO couldn't even open a connection to the model, which usually means a network outage or the model server being down.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, check the Endpoint of the Main model, and select Discover models if it's shown. If the address is wrong or unreachable, Discover models fails too, which confirms where the problem is.
  3. Once the model can be reached, check what the task already did, then send a message asking SMTO to continue from there. Changing settings or restarting doesn't give the stopped task more attempts, so continue only after the connection works.

What success looks like

  • Discover models lists your model, and SMTO replies to new messages again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the model server. Don't keep restarting SMTO to force more attempts; fix the connection first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A connection to the configured model endpoint failed (transport_connection_failed) and could not be retried automatically: either both pre-transmission retries (after 1 s and 2 s) were used up, or the failure was not a retryable DNS or connect error.

What this means

  • The transport records whether request transmission began. Only transient connection establishment failures before any request bytes permit two retries, delayed by one and two seconds. Exhaustion blocks automatic progression.

Why this can happen

  • The transport records whether request transmission began. Only transient connection establishment failures before any request bytes permit two retries, delayed by one and two seconds. Exhaustion blocks automatic progression.

How to diagnose it

  • Read request transmission evidence and the persisted retry count. Establish whether the failed operation was DNS, TCP connect, TLS or transmission before considering another attempt.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Check DNS and TCP reachability from the Server host to the Main model endpoint configured in Settings › Setup › Model routing (for example, request the endpoint's model list with curl), and read the transport facts (phase, os_error, request_bytes_sent) in the run's runtime.fault_blocked event. transport_recovery allows only two pre-transmission retries (1 s and 2 s) per run, and changing routing or restarting must not be used to reset that allowance; preserve completed work and inspect the retained retry count before continuing in a new request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check connectivity to the configured provider. Preserve completed work and inspect the retained retry count before continuing.

How to verify the fix

  • Matching evidence confirms the connection or process state.

What not to do

  • Do not reset the retry allowance by changing routing or restarting.

Technical notes

  • Do not reset the retry allowance by changing routing or restarting.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
